routes.label: Use the reciprocal definitions and double-angle rewrite

question: \(\cot10+\tan5=\)
solution:
The angles \(10\) and \(5\) have a double-angle relationship. Work in one consistent angle unit and write \(t=5\). For any \(t\) with \(\sin(2t)\ne0\), the identity \(\sin(2t)=2\sin t\cos t\) also ensures \(\cos t\ne0\). It lets us combine the two terms as
\[
\begin{aligned}
\cot(2t)+\tan t
&=\frac{\cos(2t)}{\sin(2t)}+\frac{\sin t}{\cos t}\\
&=\frac{\cos(2t)+2\sin^2t}{\sin(2t)}\\
&=\frac1{\sin(2t)}=\csc(2t),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the numerator simplifies using \(\cos(2t)=1-2\sin^2t\).

The displayed angles satisfy the denominator condition in degrees or radians. In radians, for example, \(3\pi<10<4\pi\), so \(\sin10\ne0\). Substituting \(t=5\) gives \(\boxed{\csc10}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
